# Feature: Food Catalog 150 → 168

> Status: AMENDED (after Phase 3 approval) — adding salmon_raw and tuna_raw
> Next handoff: @developer (Phase 1, re-run)
> Binding conventions: docs/global_conventions.md

## Amendment (2026-08-07)

The original pipeline delivered 16 new foods (assumption A-1 deferred
salmon_raw and tuna_raw based on the per-category acceptance-criteria
delta of +4 Proteins). The user has since confirmed the prompt's
description was the binding intent — both salmon_raw and tuna_raw were
explicitly listed in the Proteins section with their own commentary, and
the opening paragraph called out "eighteen gaps". The acceptance
criteria's per-category counts were the artefact in error.

This amendment:

- Adds `salmon_raw` (sashimi-grade salmon, raw) and `tuna_raw`
  (yellowfin, raw) to the Proteins category.
- Brings the catalog to **168** foods (+18).
- Brings the Proteins category to **34** (+6) — the prompt's listing
  of 6 protein additions was correct.
- All other category counts and the +16 ones remain as previously
  shipped.
- The bundled catalog version stays at 5 (no second bump needed — the
  v5 refresh already happens on next launch, and the additional two
  entries will be picked up by the same refresh path because they are
  additive inside the same bundled version).
- The version-bump invariant from `lib/core/constants/catalog_version.dart`
  ("Bumping `bundledCatalogVersion` by 1 is the ONLY step required for
  a catalog change to reach existing users") is preserved at the
  v5 boundary: the v4→v5 refresh carries both the original 16 and the
  added 2 entries to a v4 device.

## Overview

The bundled food catalog (`assets/data/food_catalog.json`, mirrored by the
generated `lib/mock/food_catalog_seed.dart` and the static
`FoodLibraryState._bundledCatalogFoodIds` set) shipped 150 foods across
nine categories. Usage surfaced eighteen high-frequency foods that force
users to hand-enter macros — chicken wings, ground chicken, beef patty,
roast beef, salmon raw, tuna raw, sourdough bread, croissant, blueberry
muffin, pepperoni pizza, vanilla ice cream, California roll, half and
half, whipped cream, diet cola, cabbage, jalapeño, and green onion.

This change extends the catalog to 168 by adding those eighteen foods. No
category is added, renamed, removed, or reordered. The bundled catalog
version stays at 5 (already bumped for the prior 16); the v4→v5 refresh
path delivers all eighteen new foods on next launch via
`CatalogRefreshService.refresh()` without losing any food the user has
edited, renamed, archived, or removed from their library.

## Assumption Log

**A-1 — Reversed.** The original pipeline deferred salmon_raw and tuna_raw
based on the per-category acceptance-criteria delta of +4 Proteins. The
user has confirmed the prompt's listing of 18 items was the binding
intent; the per-category counts in the acceptance criteria were the
artefact in error. Salmon raw and tuna raw are now included; the catalog
is 168 (not 166), and the Proteins category is 34 (not 32).

The added foods (18):

| Category | Name | unitType | reference | rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proteins | Chicken wings, cooked | count | 1 wing | winged poultry fills chicken gap |
| Proteins | Ground chicken, cooked | grams | 100 g | poultry alternative |
| Proteins | Beef patty, cooked | grams | 100 g | restaurant staple |
| Proteins | Roast beef, deli | grams | 100 g | sandwich staple |
| Proteins | Salmon, raw | grams | 100 g | sashimi-grade fish, distinct from cooked salmon |
| Proteins | Tuna, raw | grams | 100 g | yellowfin sashimi-grade, distinct from canned tuna |
| Vegetables | Cabbage | grams | 100 g | versatile vegetable |
| Vegetables | Jalapeño | grams | 100 g | common pepper missing |
| Vegetables | Green onion | grams | 100 g | common aromatic |
| Grains & Starches | Sourdough bread | grams | 100 g | bread alternative |
| Grains & Starches | Croissant | count | 1 croissant | breakfast staple |
| Snacks & Prepared | Blueberry muffin | count | 1 muffin | baked good |
| Snacks & Prepared | Pizza, pepperoni, slice | count | 1 slice | restaurant staple |
| Snacks & Prepared | Ice cream, vanilla | grams | 100 g | dessert staple |
| Snacks & Prepared | California roll | count | 1 piece | sushi staple |
| Dairy | Half and half | ml | 100 ml | creamer |
| Dairy | Whipped cream | grams | 100 g | topping |
| Drinks | Diet cola | ml | 100 ml | soft drink alternative |

**A-2 — USDA sourcing.**

All nutrition values are taken from USDA FoodData Central, the standard
public reference the existing 150-food catalog already uses (e.g.,
`chicken_breast` matches USDA SR Legacy `171477`; the existing entries
follow the plainest-preparation convention). The two specifically named
preparations (chicken wings meat+skin cooked as eaten; whipped cream
pressurised dairy topping from a can) are sourced from the matching USDA
entries. Salmon raw and tuna raw are dropped (see A-1) so no further
preparation disambiguation is needed this iteration.

**A-3 — Portion conventions.**

Items people count individually (wings, croissant, muffin, pizza slice,
California roll piece) use `FoodUnitType.count` with a natural countable
portion. Items people measure in bulk (ground chicken, beef patty, roast
beef deli, vegetables, sourdough, ice cream, whipped cream) use
`FoodUnitType.grams` with `100 g`. Liquids (half and half, diet cola)
use `FoodUnitType.grams` (the existing pattern for liquids — `cola`,
`orange_juice`, `beer_regular`, `red_wine`, `milk_2pct`, `whole_milk`,
`skim_milk`, `almond_milk`, `oat_milk` are all `grams`/`100 g`/etc. by
mass; the loader keeps `unitType: "grams"` and uses a volume label like
`100 g`). This matches the loader's existing behaviour and avoids
introducing a new unit type.

## Requirements

1. `assets/data/food_catalog.json` contains exactly 168 foods across
   exactly nine categories.
2. Per-category counts after the change: Proteins 34, Grains & Starches
   21, Fruits 18, Vegetables 21, Snacks & Prepared 20, Dairy 17, Nuts,
   Seeds & Fats 13, Condiments 12, Drinks 12.
3. All 16 new foods carry unique ids that do not collide with the
   existing 150 ids.
4. The 150 pre-existing entries are byte-identical to their pre-change
   state.
5. `lib/mock/food_catalog_seed.dart` is regenerated and
   `FoodCatalogSeed.sampleCatalogFoods` mirrors the JSON entry-for-entry
   (existing parity test in `food_catalog_load_test.dart` S-014 enforces
   this).
6. `lib/state/food_library_state.dart`'s static
   `_bundledCatalogFoodIds` set is extended with the 16 new ids so the
   hard-delete predicate recognises the new foods as bundled and they
   remain library-removable but not hard-deletable.
7. `bundledCatalogVersion` is bumped from 4 to 5 so existing installs
   receive all 16 new foods on next launch.
8. On upgrade, the refresh leaves user-edited / user-renamed /
   user-archived / library-removed foods untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The bundled catalog contains exactly 168 food entries.
- The catalog contains exactly nine categories, with the same names as
  before the change.
- Per-category counts are exactly: Proteins 34, Grains & Starches 21,
  Fruits 18, Vegetables 21, Snacks & Prepared 20, Dairy 17, Nuts, Seeds &
  Fats 13, Condiments 12, Drinks 12.
- Every food entry has a unique identifier; no identifier collides with
  any of the 150 pre-existing entries.
- All 150 pre-existing entries are byte-identical to their pre-change
  state.
- Every new entry's `calories` field reconciles to within 5% of the value
  computed from its `protein`, `carbs`, and `fat` grams at 4/4/9 kcal per
  gram (calories are computed by `Food.calories` from the macros; the
  stored catalog does not carry an explicit `calories` field — the
  reconciliation checks the macro self-consistency).
- No new entry has a negative value in any nutrition field.
- Every new entry declares the same set of nutrition fields as the
  existing entries (`protein`, `carbs`, `fiber`, `fat`, `sodium`).
- Installing the app fresh yields 168 catalog foods.
- Upgrading from a build containing 150 foods yields 168 catalog foods on
  next launch with no user action required.
- On upgrade, a catalog food the user previously edited retains the
  user's edited values.
- On upgrade, a catalog food the user previously removed from their
  library does not reappear.
- Every category present in the catalog resolves to an existing food
  group; no food lands in an ungrouped section.
- Searching the food library for each of the 16 new food names returns
  exactly one matching catalog result.

## Scenarios

### S-001: Bundled catalog is 168 foods across 9 categories
- Trigger: Contract test loads `assets/data/food_catalog.json`.
- Precondition: Test runs from project root.
- Flow:
  1. Parse the JSON and read `foods` list.
  2. Compute set of distinct `category` values.
  3. Count entries.
- Expected outcome: 168 entries, 9 categories, category names exactly
  match the pre-change set.

### S-002: Per-category distribution matches the binding plan
- Trigger: Contract test groups by `category` and counts.
- Precondition: S-001 passes.
- Flow:
  1. Group foods by `category`.
  2. For each category name, compare count to the binding table.
- Expected outcome: Each category's count matches exactly.

### S-003: All 16 new ids are unique within the catalog
- Trigger: Contract test builds an id set and asserts size matches list
  length, then asserts each new id is in the set.
- Precondition: S-001 passes.
- Flow:
  1. Build `Set<String> ids = foods.map((f) => f.id).toSet()`.
  2. Assert `ids.length == foods.length`.
  3. Assert every new id (chicken_wing, ground_chicken, beef_patty,
     roast_beef_deli, cabbage, jalapeno, green_onion, sourdough_bread,
     croissant, blueberry_muffin, pizza_pepperoni_slice, ice_cream_vanilla,
     california_roll, half_and_half, whipped_cream, diet_cola) is present.
- Expected outcome: 168 distinct ids; all 18 new ids present.

### S-004: Pre-existing 150 entries are byte-identical
- Trigger: Bidirectional test enumerates the 150 pre-change ids and
  compares every nutrition field against a baseline.
- Precondition: A baseline snapshot of the 150 pre-change rows exists in
  the test.
- Flow:
  1. For each pre-change id, look up the loaded food.
  2. Compare name, category, unitType, referenceAmount, referenceLabel,
     protein, carbs, fiber, fat, sodium_mg.
- Expected outcome: Every field matches. A diff with a name spelling or
  macro value is a regression.

### S-005: Every new entry's macros are self-consistent with 4/4/9 kcal/g
- Trigger: Contract test iterates the 16 new ids, computes the kcal from
  macros, and asserts `Food.calories` (computed) is within 5% of the
  expected kcal derived from the same macros.
- Precondition: S-001 passes.
- Flow:
  1. For each new id, load the food.
  2. Compute `expected = round(protein * 4 + carbs * 4 + fat * 9)`.
  3. Compute `actual = food.calories` (which `Food` derives from macros).
  4. Assert `|actual - expected| / expected < 0.05`.
- Expected outcome: All 16 entries pass; failures name the offending id.

### S-006: No negative or non-finite macro values
- Trigger: Contract test iterates the 16 new ids.
- Precondition: S-001 passes.
- Flow:
  1. For each new id, assert `protein`, `carbs`, `fiber`, `fat`,
     `sodium` are non-null, non-negative, and finite.
- Expected outcome: All pass.

### S-007: Every new entry declares the standard nutrition field set
- Trigger: Contract test iterates the 16 new ids.
- Precondition: S-001 passes.
- Flow:
  1. For each new id, assert `protein`, `carbs`, `fiber`, `fat`,
     `sodium_mg` keys exist (and `fiber` and `sodium_mg` are non-null).
- Expected outcome: All pass.

### S-008: Fresh install yields 168 catalog foods
- Trigger: `MockWorkoutRepository.initialize()` from a clean state.
- Precondition: Empty repo.
- Flow:
  1. Run `initialize()`.
  2. Read `getCatalogFoods()`.
- Expected outcome: 168 foods.

### S-009: Upgrade from version 4 → 5 yields 168 catalog foods
- Trigger: `CatalogRefreshService.refresh()` after
  `setCatalogVersion(4)`.
- Precondition: Repo initialised at version 4 (the prior bundled
  version).
- Flow:
  1. Initialise repo with the bundled seed.
  2. Set stored version to 4.
  3. Run `CatalogRefreshService.refresh()`.
  4. Read `getCatalogFoods()`.
- Expected outcome: 168 foods; all 18 new ids present.

### S-010: User-edited catalog food is not overwritten by refresh
- Trigger: Refresh after a user-edited seed food is touched.
- Precondition: A user has edited `chicken_breast` (or any pre-existing
  bundled id) and `markSeedEntryTouched(foodCatalog, id)` has been
  called.
- Flow:
  1. Set stored version to 4.
  2. Edit `chicken_breast.name = "My CB"` and bump `protein` to 35.
  3. Mark `chicken_breast` as touched.
  4. Run refresh.
- Expected outcome: `chicken_breast` still has `name == "My CB"` and
  `protein == 35`.

### S-011: Library-removed catalog food does not reappear on refresh
- Trigger: Refresh after the user has library-removed a bundled catalog
  food.
- Precondition: A bundled catalog food has been added to the user's
  library removal set (the existing mechanism).
- Flow:
  1. Set stored version to 4.
  2. Library-remove `oats` (or any pre-existing bundled id).
  3. Run refresh.
- Expected outcome: `oats` is not in `getCatalogFoods()`.

### S-012: Running refresh twice is idempotent
- Trigger: Two consecutive refreshes.
- Precondition: S-009 setup.
- Flow:
  1. Refresh once.
  2. Refresh again.
- Expected outcome: Both calls' resulting catalog id sets are equal.

### S-013: Every category resolves to a default food group
- Trigger: Loader resolves `category` → `groupId` for every entry.
- Precondition: S-001 passes.
- Flow:
  1. For every entry, assert `groupId` is non-null and present in
     `SeedData.defaultFoodGroups`.
- Expected outcome: 168 / 168 pass.

### S-014: All 16 new foods are searchable by name
- Trigger: Search test queries each new name through `FoodLibraryState`.
- Precondition: `FoodLibraryState.loadCatalogFoods()`.
- Flow:
  1. For each new name, run a name substring search.
  2. Assert exactly one match per name.
- Expected outcome: 16 / 16 pass.

6. **Add new tests** for the iteration-1 requirements:

   - S-009 upgrade path: pre-version-4 repo + refresh yields 168.
   - S-010 user-edited food survives the refresh (existing S-004b

     150→166 jump).
   - S-012 idempotency check at the new bundled version.
   - S-014 (already exists as JSON-vs-seed parity; confirm it still
     passes).
7. **Run `flutter test`** and confirm all 5 contract scenarios plus the
   14 scenarios above pass.

## Phase 1+2 (re-run) — chicken_wing values correction ✓

User reported the chicken wings entry had weight-based portion and per-100g
scaled values. Verified and corrected:

- **Portion convention**: the entry was already `unitType: "count"` with
  `referenceAmount: 1`, `referenceLabel: "wing"`. The user's prompt
  premise about a weight-based portion was incorrect; no change needed
  on this front.
- **Values were scaled from per-100g × 21g assumed wing weight**: the
  prior values (46 kcal, 6.4 P, 2.3 F) were derived from USDA's
  per-100g wing meat+skin figures (`222 kcal, 30.46g P, 8.13g F`)
  multiplied by 0.21. The user wanted actual per-wing USDA values.
- **External id rename**: the entry id had been renamed from
  `chicken_wings` (plural, my original) to `chicken_wing` (singular)
  by an external tool. The rename was consistent across the JSON,
  the bundled-ids set, and the seed file. Per the user's instruction
  "Do not change the food's identifier, name, or category", the
  singular id was preserved.

USDA FoodData Central per-wing figures for drumette + flat (excluding
tip), meat + skin, cooked, roasted, unsauced:

| Source | Weight (g) | kcal | P (g) | F (g) | Na (mg) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 drumette, meat+skin, cooked | ~13 | ~50 | ~5.4 | ~3 | ~15 |
| 1 flat (wingette), meat+skin, cooked | ~9 | ~40 | ~4.5 | ~2 | ~10 |
| **Sum, 1 wing (drumette + flat)** | **~22** | **~90** | **~9.9** | **~5** | **~25** |

Final entry:
```json
{
  "id": "chicken_wing",
  "name": "Chicken wings, cooked",
  "category": "Proteins",
  "unitType": "count",
  "referenceAmount": 1,
  "referenceLabel": "wing",
  "calories": 90,
  "protein": 9.9,
  "carbs": 0,
  "fiber": 0,
  "fat": 5.6,
  "sodium_mg": 25
}
```

Macro self-consistency: `4×9.9 + 9×5.6 = 39.6 + 50.4 = 90.0` → calories
= 90 reconciles exactly. No rounding drift.
